title: Why education matters
chinese: 人之初，性本善。性相近，习相远。
traditional: 人之初，性本善。性相近，習相遠。
pinyin: rén zhī chū, xìng běn shàn. xìng xiāng jìn, xí xiāng yuǎn.
english: At the beginning of life, human nature is good. Our natures are close, but our habits carry us far apart.
grammarPoints: Classical 之: linking or possessive particle
context: A compact literacy classic, probably composed in the 13th century. Read it as historical language and ideas—not as modern conversation.

title: The pleasure of practice
pinyin: xué ér shí xí zhī, bù yì yuè hū?
english: To learn and regularly practice what you have learned—is that not a pleasure?
context: In this famous line, 說 is read yuè and means delight. The syntax is Classical Chinese, while the core words remain useful today.

title: Learn from everyone
chinese: 三人行，必有我师焉。择其善者而从之，其不善者而改之。
traditional: 三人行，必有我師焉。擇其善者而從之，其不善者而改之。
pinyin: sān rén xíng, bì yǒu wǒ shī yān. zé qí shàn zhě ér cóng zhī, qí bù shàn zhě ér gǎi zhī.
english: When three people walk together, I can surely find a teacher among them. I follow what is good in them and use what is not good to correct myself.
grammarPoints: Classical 者: the one or aspect that…
Classical 焉 and 之 as pronouns
context: A cultural bridge into the Analects. Focus first on recognizable modern words, then notice how Classical Chinese omits information modern prose would state.

title: A universe in sixteen characters
chinese: 天地玄黄，宇宙洪荒。日月盈昃，辰宿列张。
traditional: 天地玄黃，宇宙洪荒。日月盈昃，辰宿列張。
pinyin: tiān dì xuán huáng, yǔ zhòu hóng huāng. rì yuè yíng zè, chén xiù liè zhāng.
english: The sky is dark and the earth yellow; the universe is vast and primordial. Sun and moon wax and decline; the constellations spread in ordered ranks.
grammarPoints: Classical clauses often omit linking verbs
context: A sixth-century character primer in which every character appears only once. Here 宿 is read xiù and refers to a constellation.

title: Conduct before scholarship
chinese: 弟子规，圣人训。首孝悌，次谨信。泛爱众，而亲仁。有余力，则学文。
traditional: 弟子規，聖人訓。首孝悌，次謹信。泛愛眾，而親仁。有餘力，則學文。
pinyin: dì zǐ guī, shèng rén xùn. shǒu xiào tì, cì jǐn xìn. fàn ài zhòng, ér qīn rén. yǒu yú lì, zé xué wén.
english: The standards for students transmit the sages’ teaching: begin with care for family, then act carefully and keep your word. Love people broadly and stay close to the humane; when energy remains, study literature.
context: A Qing-dynasty conduct primer. Its social values are historical rather than neutral modern advice; use it to study rhythm, compact syntax, and cultural context.

title: Knowing yourself
chinese: 知人者智，自知者明。胜人者有力，自胜者强。
traditional: 知人者智，自知者明。勝人者有力，自勝者強。
pinyin: zhī rén zhě zhì, zì zhī zhě míng. shèng rén zhě yǒu lì, zì shèng zhě qiáng.
english: One who knows others is wise; one who knows oneself is discerning. One who overcomes others has strength; one who overcomes oneself is truly strong.
grammarPoints: 者 turns a phrase into “the one who…”
context: A line from chapter 33. The repeated structure makes the contrast memorable, but the grammar and meanings are Classical Chinese.
